prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and its active form, which made possible incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: My preferred configuration is unchanged: a single-part B001 prize to Holst, Drucker and Mojsov. Round 1 did not strengthen it by agreement, because all six of us reached the same trio from the same opening rank. It is strong because the achievement is a closed arc. Proglucagon processing, the incretin effect and the active truncated peptide were followed by receptor-mediated actions on islets, gut and brain. Independent outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease then confirmed the clinical effect. The mechanism is settled and the benefit is large. The work is neither premature nor stale. A single-achievement prize also keeps all three places for people whose individual steps are each necessary to the physiology. I have made one change to my reasoning, not to the configuration. I now state the Knudsen question as a deliberate allocation under the three-person cap, not as a distinction between discovery and development.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness. Knudsen's acylation and half-life engineering turned a peptide with a half-life of minutes into a once-weekly drug, and a physiology-only citation can be read as honouring the hormone and not the therapy. Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) form relative to Habener's group cannot be settled from the files in front of us. The chair asked whether we can state the priority split from citable documents, and I cannot. The supplied material does not contain the primary publications, so any statement I made would come from general knowledge. My view is that this should be treated as an open question and stated as one, not resolved by assertion. If the committee concludes that the priority record on the active peptide is too unclear to name Mojsov, the fallback I would accept is a narrower physiology citation to Holst and Drucker, or a trio with Knudsen. I would not simply substitute Habener without the primary record.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius says that engineering a native peptide into a once-weekly drug is a scientific achievement and not routine development, and that she keeps Knudsen out because three places force a choice. She would hesitate most on Mojsov.
responses.response: You are right, and I withdraw my round-1 phrasing that placed her work outside discovery. Half-life engineering by acylation is a conceptually new solution, and it is what reached patients. I still keep the trio on the physiology side, for the reason you give: the cap forces a choice, and the physiology and active-peptide steps are what every later analogue depends on. I do not accept that this makes Mojsov the weakest place. Her role concerns the identity and activity of the peptide that all therapeutic design targets, so omitting her would leave the citation's phrase 'its active form' without a named discoverer. I would put the burden on any substitution to show whose step in that chain is replaced. I would consider Knudsen in place of one of the three only if the committee decides the drug is the achievement and the citation is drafted around it.

responses.point: Linnarsson argues that Nobel recognition has honoured translational steps when they were conceptually new, but lands on the basic trio, and says Mojsov's priority should be pressed as a real open question.
responses.response: I agree with the method of your argument. Treating Mojsov's priority as open does not weaken the case for B001, and the committee should say so in its minutes. The practical consequence is that the citation should not rest on a claim of first identification. The wording 'physiology of GLP-1 and its active form' describes the discovery that made the drugs possible, without asserting a priority ruling that we cannot document. I differ from you slightly on confidence. I do not think an unresolved priority question is enough to drop her, because the evidence that the truncated peptide was the active insulinotropic form comes from several sources, and the record I know of gives her a substantial place in it. I flag again that this is general knowledge. If a documented source contradicted it, my position on the third name would change, and I would say so in the final ballot.

responses.point: Perlmann disagrees that the omission of the eIF2alpha/PERK arm is a minor simplification for B051. A Walter and Mori pair would define the prize around IRE1 and HAC1/XBP1 and leave out the integrated stress response, so he ranks B051 below CAR-T and optogenetics this year.
responses.response: I concede the point. In round 1 I called the omission a simplification, and I now think it is a real gap in the citation. A Walter and Mori prize honours the IRE1-HAC1/XBP1 pathway and its conceptual novelty, which is a clean discovery with a clean pair. A reader who equates 'the unfolded protein response' with the whole signalling network would still see a prize that leaves out the PERK arm. That is a defensible narrow citation, but it is not a complete account. With early clinical translation, it does not justify placing B051 ahead of the clinically validated candidates, and I have moved it from my second to my second-listed alternative behind B017. I keep it as an alternative because the attribution is the cleanest on the shortlist, and the committee may value that if B001 stalls. My RNA-processing background overlaps with the HAC1 splicing mechanism, and I have disclosed that as shared subject matter.

responses.point: Svenningsson regards the June and Sadelain split as a fair reading of who designed and validated clinically effective CARs. He would not exclude Rosenberg lightly because adoptive transfer and early engineered-T-cell trials are part of the lineage.
responses.response: I accept that my exclusion of Rosenberg depends on a particular definition of the achievement. If it is 'genetically engineered CAR-T cells', then June and Sadelain designed and validated the receptors, and Rosenberg's work is best described as adoptive transfer plus early engineered-cell trials. If the committee instead credits the lineage that made engineered T-cell therapy possible, Rosenberg belongs, and Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept would then be a stronger claim than I allowed. I cannot resolve this from the shortlist entry, and because the attribution depends on how the achievement is worded, I prefer B017 as an alternative and not as my preferred configuration. If B001 stalls, B017 is the configuration I would work on first, and I would want the committee to agree the citation wording before it chose the names. On B050, I accept your point on timing: the mechanism is crisp, but absent established clinical impact it should wait.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's priority for the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide can be documented well enough to name her without reservation, and whether Habener or others outside the credited list have an equal claim. I cannot settle this from the supplied files and rely on general knowledge.

Whether the committee should draft the B001 citation around the physiology and the active peptide or around the drug-development arm. Knudsen's inclusion would change the achievement, not only the name list.
Whether a single-part B001 prize is better than a two-part prize. I prefer one part, but I have not tested a second part against the three-person limit.

For B017, whether the achievement is the CAR design (June, Sadelain) or the wider lineage that includes Rosenberg and the early receptor work of Eshhar. For B051, whether a Walter and Mori pair is an acceptable narrow citation given the missing PERK arm.
How much weight clinical translation should carry against mechanistic discovery for B051 and B050. I would apply the same standard to B012, which has not changed patient care.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from my profile for the preferred configuration. I have co-authored with Sten Linnarsson and Jonas Frisén and share a KI setting with them, and none of that touches B001, B017 or B051. My RNA-processing background overlaps with the HAC1/XBP1 splicing mechanism in B051 and with B040, as shared subject matter and not a personal tie. I have no documented connection to any named candidate, and this disclosure is unchanged from round 1.
